budget_tradeoff_detail: none — uses GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k window but no reported token-cost-vs-quality tradeoff numbers
confound_note: RQ4 ablation (vanilla vs. local-only vs. local+global vs. all-three) varies which knowledge types are injected into the prompt; token budget is not held constant as an independent variable (Sec. V-D)
stop_detail: Local-aware context via AST parsing of the current file, global-aware context via dual textual+semantic embedding retrieval over other repo files, third-party context via AST-extracted imports, all fused into the generation prompt (Sec. III-B)
threats_to_datum: custom reuse-awareness precision/recall/F1 metric is study-specific and not directly comparable to pass@1-style metrics used elsewhere in the literature

budget_tradeoff_detail: selective retrieval trades ~16-28% (threshold-based) up to ~69-70% (greedy, API completion) latency reduction for comparable or improved ES/pass-rate vs. an always-retrieve baseline (Table 3, Sec 5.3)
confound_note: central ablation (Table 5) varies whether/when retrieval fires and the training objective (multi-task with self-eval loss vs. without), not a fixed context budget across arms; retrieved-context size (~512 tokens, top-10 Jaccard-similarity chunks) is held constant whenever retrieval does occur
stop_detail: Model emits a special <cc> token to trigger Jaccard-similarity top-k chunk retrieval from the repo, or emits nothing to skip retrieval and complete from local context alone, via a self-supervised learned gate (Sec 3.2-3.3)
threats_to_datum: speedup figures are reported for specific completion types/model sizes (e.g., greedy API completion, 1B model) and may not generalize across all benchmark splits

key_numbers.metric: Best combined (RAG + static analysis) Java Line EM

budget_tradeoff_detail: in-file context truncated to 2,000 tokens and cross-file context to 3,000 tokens (Sec 4.5); prompting-phase integration adds full hierarchical static-analysis info on top of these truncated baselines, so token counts differ systematically across strategies
confound_note: central comparison varies both the static-analysis integration point (prompting/decoding/post-processing phase) and the resulting prompt content/length simultaneously — budget is not held constant across arms
stop_detail: Static analysis extracts a hierarchical file-level skeleton (module→class→signature/members) and token-level valid-identifier lists, injected either into the prompt (prompting phase, Sec 3.1), via logit masking at decoding (Sec 3.2), or via candidate filtering post-generation (Sec 3.3)
threats_to_datum: best-performing integration combination differs by language (Java: prompting+decoding; Python: prompting+post-processing), so headline numbers do not generalize across languages

benchmarks: 8 OSS-Fuzz projects: c-ares, cjson, curl, lcms, libpcap, libtiff, libvpx, zlib

key_numbers.metric: Average code coverage improvement vs. SOTA

budget_tradeoff_detail: none — no token/cost budget figures reported; the graph retrieval returns a fixed number of relevant chunks but count/token size is not quantified
confound_note: Table II ablation simultaneously varies presence of the repair mechanism, LLM-only vs. KG-based repair, and text-only vs. graph retrieval — not a token-normalized, single-factor comparison
stop_detail: Code Knowledge Graph (function/file nodes; CONTAINS/CALLS/LIBRARY_CALLS edges) built via Tree-sitter + CodeQL interprocedural analysis; a retrieval-augmented agent queries the graph for relevant chunks during API-combination generation and coverage-guided mutation (Sec III-B/III-C, Algorithm 1)
threats_to_datum: exact SOTA comparators for the 8.73% coverage improvement are not detailed in the accessible text; per-project coverage varies widely (22-84%), so the average masks heterogeneity

demote_reason: Full text confirms RTL++ operates exclusively on single, self-contained RTL modules (100-300 LOC) with inter-module dependencies explicitly embedded into or filtered out of each module (Sec III-A/III-B). The CFG/DFG graph representations are used only to construct fine-tuning training data (Sec III-D) and are never retrieved or budgeted at inference time; there is no cross-file/repository scope, no context-window budget management, and no retrieval mechanism anywhere in the paper — it is a training-data augmentation technique for single-module code generation, not repository-level context engineering.

benchmarks: 6 GitHub projects: lucene, poi, jgit, itext, quartz, rocketmq-clients (Java<->C# pairs)
budget_tradeoff_detail: none — no token/cost numbers reported despite iterative multi-agent tool calls
confound_note: Table IV component ablation removes whole agents (RAG/Context/Refine) at once, conflating retrieval mechanism with prompt construction and iterative refinement — not an isolated representation-only or budget-only comparison
stop_detail: Context Agent iteratively calls JSON-returning lookup tools (class info, imports, method bodies) informed by hybrid dense+BM25 RAG retrieval with reciprocal-rank fusion, gathering context until sufficient before translation (Sec III-B/III-C)
threats_to_datum: baseline comparators (UniTrans, PLTranslation) are prior published tools potentially evaluated under different exact splits; component ablation confounds multiple mechanisms per arm

benchmarks: Code Context Competition (Kotlin and Python tracks)
budget_tradeoff_detail: claims GPU/embedding-hosting cost is avoided entirely by using keyword search instead of semantic embeddings, but no explicit token or dollar-cost numbers are given
confound_note: compares keyword-search retrieval against the (unspecified) field of Code Context Competition entries; representation, retriever, and likely compute budget all differ simultaneously across competing systems
stop_detail: Uses keyword/lexical search (not dense embeddings) over the codebase to select code context fed to a completion model, avoiding GPU-hosted embedding models (Abstract; full method section unavailable — HTML/ar5iv rendering returned 404)
threats_to_datum: full paper text was unavailable (404 on both arxiv.org/html and ar5iv); numbers taken from abstract/metadata only, exact retrieval algorithm and comparison baselines not independently verified

budget_tradeoff_detail: reports the central token-budget-vs-fidelity tradeoff directly: a 239k-token repository is compressed to 11k tokens (18:1) while maintaining 94-97% task success across 12 models, claimed to outperform flat/uncompressed context methods
confound_note: comparison is 'flat methods' vs. hierarchical TREEFRAG compression — representation and budget change simultaneously (compression is itself the budget reduction), so this is not a budget-held-constant ablation; full methodology and baseline details unverified since full text was unreachable
stop_detail: Hierarchical tree-based 'TREEFRAG' decomposition compresses a full repository into a compact structured summary retained in the prompt, per Abstract (full-text method section unavailable — 404 on both arxiv.org/html and ar5iv)
threats_to_datum: single-author preprint with no stated institutional affiliation, no peer review, and full text unreachable — facet codes above are inferred from the abstract only and should be treated as low-confidence

budget_tradeoff_detail: CCE yields +5.79pp external SPR / +8.24pp internal APR / up to +7.56pp overall improvement at roughly comparable or lower per-instance cost than plain agentic exploration ($0.1241 vs $0.1226 on ReCUBE; $0.1166 vs $0.1410 on ReCUBE-large, Table 7), while full-context baselines consume 71K-146K tokens on average
confound_note: central comparison (full-context vs. agent vs. agent+CCE) varies representation, retrieval mechanism, and effective context length/cost together — not a fixed-budget ablation; caller-graph availability, agent tool access, and token consumption all differ simultaneously across arms
stop_detail: Caller-Centric Exploration (CCE) toolkit exposes a heterogeneous directed graph (dir/file/class/function nodes; contain/import/invoke/inherit edges) via caller-pattern, graph-query, and validation tools that steer agentic exploration before/during masked-file reconstruction (Sec 4.2.2/4.3)
threats_to_datum: benchmark authored concurrently with the proposed CCE method (possible self-benchmarking bias); context-window differences across models (131K-400K) confound cross-model comparisons

budget_tradeoff_detail: no token-budget-vs-quality tradeoff reported; only a fixed max-step budget of 250 actions is held constant across conditions (Sec A.2), and perturbations increase file-access ratio 2.49x-5.77x without a corresponding token accounting
confound_note: RepoMirage-Perturb/Extend vary how repository structure is exposed (import indirection, file renaming/relocation, constant externalization) while holding the underlying task fixed; the RepoAnchor comparison then adds an explicit structure-exploration stage, changing both mechanism and effective context organization at once
stop_detail: Three semantics-preserving perturbations (dependency-path indirection, runtime-target masking, local-value externalization) obscure direct repo cues, forcing broader agent exploration; RepoAnchor separates structure exploration from code construction via an intermediate INSTRUCTIONS.md artifact (Sec 3.1, 5.3)
threats_to_datum: success-rate drop conflates increased task difficulty from perturbation with genuine failure of context-reasoning; the fixed 250-step budget may itself bind harder for perturbed conditions requiring more file access

benchmarks: SWE-Review-Bench (1,384 PRs from 500 SWE-bench Verified issues)
budget_tradeoff_detail: Opus 4.6 achieves the highest decision accuracy (81.8%) using only ~148K tokens on average vs. 2.09-2.36M tokens for smaller distilled reviewer models, and review-guided iterative revision reaches 38.4% resolve rate using only 2.44 samples on average vs. 8.9 for reviewer-gated resampling (Table 5, Fig 5, Appendix B.3)
confound_note: single-turn diff-only vs. diff+context vs. full agentic-review arms vary both the context-gathering mechanism and how much/what context is seen; the paper explicitly attributes gains to adaptive evidence-gathering rather than sheer context volume (Sec 3.2), but arms are not budget-matched
stop_detail: Reviewer agent (OpenHands-SDK scaffold) agentically browses files, greps code, inspects dependencies, and executes reproducer commands in the repo to decide accept/request-changes and produce structured revision feedback in a generate-review-revise loop (Sec 3.1, Table 5)
threats_to_datum: PR-generator distributions used to build SWE-Review-Bench (GLM-5, Qwen3-Coder-30B, Qwen3-30B) differ substantially in baseline resolve rate (27.5-72.2%), so aggregate review-correctness numbers mix heterogeneous PR quality

budget_tradeoff_detail: OpenCoder matches baseline RAG's five-candidate generation budget and at-most-two repair rounds exactly, isolating uncertainty-aware filtering/ranking as the sole varied factor; the +21.88pp gain (GPT, selected-output correctness) is attributable to the mechanism, not extra budget — though OpenCoder ties RAG+Verify/Repair at 78.13%, so the advantage vanishes once verification/repair is added (RQ3)
confound_note: RQ3's three arms (Baseline RAG, RAG+Verify/Repair, OpenCoder) hold retrieval evidence and candidate/repair budgets constant, varying only whether uncertainty-aware filtering/ranking/repair is applied — a genuine budget-matched comparison; however the Gemini backend shows no statistically supported gain, indicating the effect is backend-dependent
stop_detail: Uncertainty-aware framework retrieves API-knowledge, repository-context, and similar-code evidence via UniXcoder embeddings (up to 8 candidates each), scores it by combining token entropy, self-consistency, and semantic variance (weights 0.4/0.4/0.2) to filter/rank evidence before conditioning generation, verification, and repair (Problem Formulation, Eq. 1-9)
threats_to_datum: small benchmark (32 tasks); statistical significance holds for the GPT backend only (Gemini result not significant); the name 'OpenCoder' collides with the unrelated pre-existing OpenCoder LLM project, risking citation confusion
